name: Superhuman
look: Three-canvas system — indigo navy hero, white body, deep teal closing band — with sub-default type weights and 0.96 line-heights.

hero.title: The fastest email experience ever made
hero.sub: Blazingly fast, keyboard-first, and built so that reaching inbox zero takes twenty minutes rather than the whole morning. Most people save four hours a week.

features.title: Designed around the keyboard
features.sub: Every hundred milliseconds you spend waiting is a hundred milliseconds of attention you do not get back.

items.title: Command palette
items.body: Every action two keystrokes away. The mouse becomes optional rather than merely discouraged.

items.title: Under 100ms
items.body: Every interaction, measured at the ninety-fifth percentile — not the median on a good connection.

items.title: Split inbox
items.body: Important mail separated from newsletters and automated noise, by rules you can actually read.

items.title: Snippets
items.body: Expand a whole reply from three characters, with placeholders you tab between.

items.title: Read statuses
items.body: See whether a message was opened, and on what, without a third-party tracker.

items.title: Team comments
items.body: Discuss a thread alongside it, without a forward chain or a separate channel.

showcases.title: A hundred milliseconds, every time
showcases.body: The target is not an average — it is the ninety-fifth percentile of every interaction, on ordinary hardware. Mail is prefetched, the index is local, and rendering never waits on the network.
points: Works on a plane, syncs on landing

showcases.title: Discuss a thread beside it
showcases.body: Comments live alongside the message rather than in a forward chain nobody can reconstruct later. The person who inherits the account in six months can still see why the decision was made.

metric_lead: Reported by users after ninety days

gallery.title: Inside Swift
gallery.sub: A look at the surfaces you will spend your morning in.

testimonial.quote: I stopped dreading Monday mornings. That is an absurd thing to say about an email client and it is also the honest reason I still pay for it three years later.
testimonial.name: Elena Vasquez

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: One plan for individuals, one for teams. Thirty days free, no card.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.desc: For teams working the same inboxes.

items.q: Does it work with my email?
items.a: Gmail and Outlook, including Workspace and Microsoft 365 accounts. Other IMAP providers are not supported, because the speed depends on provider-specific sync behaviour.
No. Mail is indexed on your device. Server-side we hold metadata needed for sync and search, encrypted at rest, and the security page states exactly what that includes.
They use a pixel, and they are off by default per-message. Recipients running standard image blocking will not register — we do not attempt to work around that.
Yes, for iOS and Android, with the same split inbox and snippets. The keyboard-first parts obviously matter less there.

cta.title: Get four hours back this week
cta.sub: Thirty days free, no card required, and your existing mail stays exactly where it is.

footer.tagline: The fastest email experience ever made.

notes: Three canvases carry the page: indigo navy for the hero, white for the body, deep teal for the closing CTA. They are never blended into each other.
The hero uses a half-bleed portrait against a violet-sky backdrop — a person looking off-frame is the recurring brand image.
One CTA per band. The marketing pages never put two competing actions in the same section.
Type sits at sub-default weights (460, 540, 600), which is where the typographic warmth comes from. Rounding those to 500/600/700 loses it.
Display line-height compresses to 0.96, and body ink is a warm off-grey (#292827) rather than black.
